newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean banker arrested on bribery charge.
newsitem.headline: South Korean banker arrested on bribery charge.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors said they arrested the president of SEOULBANK on bribery charges Saturday.
Sohn Hong-gyun, 60, was charged with accepting $121,000 in return for providing loans to a South Korean company, a prosecution spokesman said.
Sohn is the latest prominent figure in South Korea to be arrested in an anti-corruption drive spearheaded by President Kim Young-sam.
Fourteen other bank heads have been either arrested or fired for involvement in corruption scandals since Kim took office in 1993.
Last month, Kim dismissed his defence minister, Lee Yang-ho, who was formally charged last week with accepting bribes and leaking secrets in connection with arms procurement.

The prosecution spokesman said Sohn was accused of "arranging loans in excess of the legal limits" in return for bribes from a valve manufacturing company. The head of the company is being questioned, he said.
